key_insight: DeltaBox achieves millisecond-level sandbox checkpoint/rollback by capturing and applying compact deltas of file and process state combined with copy-on-write memory remapping, avoiding full-state duplication on each checkpoint.
problem_solved: Existing C/R mechanisms duplicate entire sandbox states (files, memory, process contexts), causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency per checkpoint/rollback and bottlenecking high-frequency state exploration for LLM-powered agents (e.g., test-time tree search, RL, large fan-outs).
method: Delta (incremental) checkpoints: only record changed pages/bytes and metadata between successive snapshots to minimize data written.
Kernel-assisted copy-on-write and memory remapping: clone sandbox address spaces and lazily materialize modified pages to enable near-instant clones and rollbacks.
Unified file+process snapshot layer with lazy restoration: combine filesystem diffs and process-state descriptors so rollbacks restore consistent end-to-end sandbox state with minimal I/O.
impact: Millisecond C/R lets AI agents explore many more hypothetical branches and parallel rollouts with lower latency and resource cost, enabling deeper search, faster RL iterations, and larger-scale fan-outs in production agent systems.
visual_elements: Latency comparison bar chart: full duplication vs DeltaBox (seconds → milliseconds).
Architecture diagram: delta capture, COW memory remap, unified snapshot/restore pipeline.

paper_title: DeltaBox: Scaling Stateful AI Agents with Millisecond-Level Sandbox Checkpoint/Rollback
paper_authors: Yunpeng Dong, Jingkai He, Yuze Hou, Dong Du, Zhonghu Xu
